name: all-1
statement: The cued base and Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math have nearly the same per-step math skill; the residual gap is a long-horizon self-conditioning deficit, in which the base's next-token distribution degrades as its own generated solution grows (loops at T 0.6, unfinished drift at T 1.0). Olmo-3.1's RL, which trained truncated rollouts as negatives at 16k, repaired this with a diffuse weight direction that changes activations only deep inside long math contexts, so the gap scales with solution length and token budget, not with problem knowledge.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base (with and without the opening cue) vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math and Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0), MATH-500 and the 328 harder problems, T 0.6-1.0, caps 4k-32k, weight interpolation base + a*(RL - base). It does not cover the plain (uncued) base's format failures, the Code pair, or pass@k ceilings.

explains.how: The 3.0 RL model, trained without truncation negatives, only equals the cued base (77.9), so the extra 3.1 gain comes from the change in how truncated long rollouts were trained.

explains.quote: not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives)
explains.how: This is the training signal that penalises failing to finish a long generation, which is the deficit the theory names.

explains.quote: from RL's prefix 48 / 41 / 21; from its own prefix 23 / 16 / 38
explains.how: On the same problems the base finishes twice as often from RL's sound prefix as from its own, so its failure is in conditioning on its own long text, not in missing knowledge.

explains.quote: T1 cap hits exceed T2's by 15.2 points in Q4
explains.how: The gap and the excess cap hits concentrate in the longest-solution quartile, as a length-dependent hazard predicts.
On longer, harder problems the base runs out of budget nearly 4x as often as RL at the same tokens per problem.
At T 0.6 the same deficit shows up as repetition attractors in the base's own long context.

explains.quote: diverge on math solutions, more with depth
explains.how: The RL change leaves general-text activations untouched and shows only in long math generations, where self-conditioning matters.
Even at T 1.0 a quarter of the RL-only items are base answers that drift without finishing, not loops.

explains.quote: the gain is more answers finishing under the cap
explains.how: An independent model shows the same pattern: a no-training change raises MATH-500 by making more answers finish, not by raising accuracy on finished answers.

conflicts.how: The shortest-solution quartile already has an 11-point gap, which a pure length-dependent deficit should not produce.

conflicts.quote: finished with a wrong answer on 33
conflicts.how: Most RL-only hard problems are base answers that finished wrong, not unfinished ones; the theory must claim these are drift errors late in long answers.
Misreads and slips look like per-step errors, not long-context degradation.

conflicts.quote: the top 4 % of positions carry 38.7 % of KL
conflicts.how: The theory predicts KL concentrated late in long answers; this readout does not report position, so it is untested rather than a direct conflict.

rival: RL improved the policy at each step (a stopping-and-verification rule or better choices at fork tokens) uniformly over positions. Separation: the rival predicts KL(RL||base) per token on RL's own long answers is flat over position, that RL leads at every token cap, and that Olmo-3.0 RL (same steps, no truncation negatives) is about as good as 3.1 at T 1.0. This theory predicts KL rising with position, the gap closing or reversing at a 4k cap, and 3.0 well below 3.1.

predictions.experiment: Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release), plain prompt, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, MATH-500 one sample
predictions.refuted_by: 3.0 scores 440 or more, close to 3.1's 463, or has fewer cap hits than 3.1

predictions.experiment: Teacher-forced KL(RL||base) per token after the cue on RL's own T 1.0 MATH-500 answers longer than 8,000 tokens; ratio of mean KL in the last quarter of positions to the first quarter
predictions.refuted_by: ratio below 1.2 (KL flat or falling with position)

predictions.experiment: Existing T 1.0 MATH-500 answers of the cued base (410) and RL (463) rescored with every answer truncated at 4,096 generated tokens (an unfinished answer counts wrong); RL minus cued base
predictions.refuted_by: RL leads the cued base by more than 2 points at the 4,096 cap

predictions.experiment: Base continues at T 1.0 from the first 40 % of RL's right answer vs from the first 40 % of its own answer, on the base's 77 hard-328 cap-hit problems with the cue; difference in finish rate (no cap hit)
base + 0.5*(RL - base) with the cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, hard 328, grader v3, one sample; cap hits
predictions.refuted_by: cap hits stay at 70 or more (the base's 77) while accuracy rises above 175
